title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. L is a totally ordered set. M is a family of bounded 'intervals' X of L, each with:
- a boundary δX (its endpoints), and
- an underlying set or position |X|.

M̂ enlarges M by the open rays I_{<a} and I_{>b} (and the intervals I_{ω0,a} discussed on the previous page). M is apparently equipped with two relations: a strong containment X' ⊂⊂ X (variants with a superscript °) and a separation relation |∘|. The axioms are called Mag 1–4.

The page extends the order relation ≤ from M to M̂ by the rule
  X ≤ Y ⟺ (1°) δX ≤ δY, i.e. every endpoint of X is ≤ every endpoint of Y; and
          (2°) a ray can only be compared 'from the outside':
               (a) if Y = I_{<a} then X = Y;
               (b) if X = I_{>a} then Y = X.
Read geometrically, ≤ means 'X lies to the left of Y'. A left ray has nothing strictly to its left, and a right ray has nothing strictly to its right.

Consequences noted on the page:
- X ≤ Y ⇒ |X| ≤ |Y|, and X < Y ⇒ |X| < |Y|.
- I_{>a} ≤ I_{<b} never holds.
- I_{<a} ≤ I_{>b} ⟺ a ≤ b.

The separation relation on M̂ is then defined as
  X |·| Y ⟺ X < Y or Y < X,
i.e. {X,Y} is a 2-element flag (Dra_{1/2}, 'drapeaux') of the poset (M̂, ≤). So two regions are 'separated' when they are strictly comparable, meaning one lies entirely to the left of the other.

Verification of the axioms:
- Mag 1 and Mag 2 are declared OK.
- Mag 3 (separation passes to strongly-contained subregions) follows from: X < Y, X' ⊂⊂ X, Y' ⊂⊂ Y ⇒ X' ≤ Y', refined to X' < Y' except in degenerate equality cases.
- Mag 4 is declared clear.

Purpose. This builds a completion M̂ ⊇ M of a 'Mag' structure of intervals of a totally ordered set. The next page proves that M is 'très dense' in M̂: separation in M̂ is detected on strongly-contained elements of M. Its corollary is that the supports (points, Σ) of M̂ and M agree.

This is a point-free / region-based description of the ordered line, in which points are recovered as supports from regions plus separation and strong-containment relations.
errors: The first Mag 3 line reads 'X ≤ Y, X' ⊂⊂° X, Y' ⊂⊂° Y ⇒ X' < Y''. With X = Y this is false: two subregions of the same interval need not be strictly ordered. The ≤ appears overwritten (bold) and should read X < Y. The second line ('X<Y … ⇒ X'≤Y'', then refined) is the corrected version.

In the NB, 'X ≤ Y ⇒ |X| ≤ |Y|' only makes sense with X = Y if |X| ≤ |Y| is a non-strict comparison of positions or endpoints rather than 'all elements ≤' for sets. The meaning of |·| is ambiguous on this page.
Clause 2°(a)/(b) is stated asymmetrically. It is consistent with the 'left of' reading, but the first draft wrote it with X and Y swapped and Grothendieck corrected it.

ideas.what: Completion of a structure of intervals of a totally ordered set by adding open rays I_{<a}, I_{>b}, with an order 'X entirely left of Y' defined via boundaries plus special rules for rays
ideas.modern_name: end-compactification / Dedekind-type completion of an interval structure; region-based (point-free) model of the line

ideas.what: Separation (disjointness/apartness) relation defined as strict comparability, i.e. 2-element flags of the poset
ideas.modern_name: comparability / apartness relation; 'precedence' in interval orders

ideas.what: Axioms 'Mag 1–4' linking strong containment ⊂⊂ and separation; checking that M̂ satisfies them and (next page) that M is 'very dense' in M̂, so supports coincide
ideas.modern_name: close to proximity/contact algebras and mereotopology (regions, well-inside relation, points as derived objects)
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Laguna, Whitehead, Tarski (mereotopology); Efremovič (proximity spaces); de Vries (compingent algebras); Düntsch–Vakarelov (contact algebras)

missed.claim: The 'Mag' axiom system is a Grothendieck-original point-free framework: regions with strong containment ⊂⊂ and a separation relation, with points (supports Σ) recovered from regions and invariance under very dense substructures. It parallels de Vries / contact-algebra / mereotopological approaches, which the literature does not connect to Grothendieck. This page is only a routine verification inside that framework.
missed.quote: X|·|Y ⟺ X<Y ou Y<X i.e. {X,Y} ∈ Dra_{1/2}(M̂,≤). Vérification des axiomes. Mag 1 OK, Mag 2 OK, Mag 3 OK
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If the full Mag axiomatics (defined on earlier pages of cote 156-9) amount to a distinct region-based topology, they could be compared with contact algebras and locale theory. The present page alone carries little new content.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine checking of axioms for a ray-completion of an interval structure on an ordered set. Its only interest is as evidence of a 1986 point-free / region-based axiomatics ('Mag') that is not in the published record. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.
transcription_corrections: Top line: the inserted '(X ≠ Y ∧)' with '7' above appears to belong to a struck-out first definition, roughly 'X < Y ⟺ (X≠Y ∧ |X| ≤ |Y|)'. The bold symbol in 'X ⊆ Y' at the top looks like an overwritten '<'.
Mag 3 first line: the bold '≤' in 'X ≤ Y, X' ⊂⊂° X' appears overwritten and should probably be read as '<'.
Last refinement line likely reads '↪ X' < Y' ou X' = X = Y' ou Y', i.e. degenerate equality cases, rather than 'ex X'.
Margin letter 'M' before the definition of ≤ is a marker for the definition, not part of a formula.
'Dra_{1/2}' is most plausibly 'Dra_{1/2}' = drapeaux (2-element flags/chains) of the poset.
